system.en: Under this system, Poland had to rebuild, and especially they had to rebuild Warsaw.
system.zh: 在这种体制下，波兰必须进行重建，特别是他们必须重建华沙。

system.en: Under the new system, settlement is something you earn, not something you automatically receive.
system.zh: 在新系统下，定居是你挣来的，而不是自动获得的。

system.en: They created a calendar system and they made significant advances in astronomy and mathematics.
system.zh: 他们创建了历法系统，并在天文学和数学方面取得了重大进展。

system.en: Saudi Arabia could adopt a different system that kept things in the same generation.
system.zh: 沙特阿拉伯可以采用一种将权力保持在同一代人手中的不同体制。

system.en: This is the reality of the Crown Court system in England and Wales in 2026.
system.zh: 这就是2026年英格兰和威尔士刑事法院系统的现实状况。

symbol.en: These seals often show animals and symbols, which appears to be a writing system.
symbol.zh: 这些印章通常显示动物和符号，这似乎是一种书写系统。

symbol.en: Over time, Christ the Redeemer has become, I guess, the global symbol of Brazil.
symbol.zh: 随着时间推移，基督救世主雕像已经成为我猜想的巴西全球象征。

symbol.en: Cuneiform symbols were pressed into soft clay tablets using a stylus, like a stick.
symbol.zh: 楔形文字符号是用触笔（类似于小棍子）压印在软泥板上的。

symbol.en: Sorry, I’ve mispronounced it probably. Another famous symbol in the city is the Warsaw mermaid.
symbol.zh: 抱歉，我可能发音不准。城中的另一个著名标志是华沙人鱼。

symbol.en: Over time, the Berlin Wall became the symbol of the Cold War.
symbol.zh: 随着时间的推移，柏林墙成为了冷战的象征。

symptom.en: She mentions feeling tired, having a headache or a dry mouth as symptoms of dehydration.
symptom.zh: 她提到感到疲劳、头痛或口干是脱水的症状。

symptom.en: And then when he was describing some of the symptoms, I was like, huh?
symptom.zh: 我朋友先被诊断出来，告诉了我，这改变了他的一生。

symptom.en: Symptoms are signs or feelings in the body showing the presence of some illness or condition.
symptom.zh: 症状是身体上显示某种疾病或身体状况存在的迹象或感觉。

symptom.en: These are not the symptoms of a blood disease; they are the hallmarks of severe mania.
symptom.zh: 这些都不是血液疾病的症状；它们是严重躁狂症的标志。

symptom.en: They had emphasised the physical symptoms and quietly downplayed, or simply omitted, the psychiatric ones.
symptom.zh: 他们强调了身体症状，而悄悄淡化甚至直接忽略了精神症状。

systematic.en: All right, so you actually looked in a fairly systematic, empirical way at baseball players.
systematic.zh: 好的，所以你实际上以一种相当系统、实证的方式研究了棒球运动员。

systematic.en: A systematic review of George's actual medical records found that the two researchers had been highly selective.
systematic.zh: 对 George 实际病历的系统性审查发现，那两位研究人员进行了高度的选择性摘录。

systematic.en: Do you think you could have got there had you have not done the procedural, systematic, sort of step by step by step, this is what it is, and then come out the other side?
systematic.zh: 你觉得如果你没有经历过那种程序化的、系统的、一步步来的过程，然后从另一端走出来，你能达到现在的境界吗？

systematically.en: And then it was logic: the art of reason, evaluating statements logically and systematically.
systematically.zh: 接着是逻辑学：推理的艺术，合乎逻辑且系统地评估陈述。

systematically.en: Jewish people and other persecuted groups were systematically excluded from public life.
systematically.zh: 犹太人和其他受迫害的群体被系统地排挤出公众生活。

systematically.en: It can be genuinely, systematically, brutal.
systematically.zh: 它可以是真真切切、有组织、有体系的残暴。

systematically.en: In his twenties, he worked as a buffalo hunter on the Kansas plains, when the vast herds that had roamed the great plains for centuries were being systematically slaughtered for their hides.
systematically.zh: 二十多岁时，他在堪萨斯平原上当过猎捕野牛的猎人，当时那些在大平原上漫游了几个世纪的庞大兽群，正被有计划地大批猎杀以获取兽皮。

sympathetic.en: Virgil Earp, as Tombstone’s town marshal, was not sympathetic to the Cowboys at all.
sympathetic.zh: 身为汤姆斯通镇治安官的 Virgil Earp，对“牛仔帮”完全没有半分好感。

sympathetic.en: The county sheriff, a man named Johnny Behan, was sympathetic to the Cowboys.
sympathetic.zh: 县警长 Johnny Behan 对“牛仔帮”抱有同情。

sympathetic.en: You guys are much more sympathetic. And it might be just because we're reporters, and you want to make us think you're good guys, but you're really cold-hearted.
sympathetic.zh: 你们显得更有同情心。这可能只是因为我们是记者，而你想让我们觉得你们是好人，但实际上你们铁石心肠。

sympathy.en: It's a very unique category of challenge because the total addressable market for sympathy is basically zero.
sympathy.zh: 这是一个非常独特的挑战类别，因为同情的潜在市场几乎为零。

sympathy.en: Like, do you want sympathy? Because I will happily give you sympathy.
sympathy.zh: 你是想要同情吗？因为我很乐意给你同情。

sympathy.en: Whether they had earned that right. Whether their sympathy was real, or whether it was something more convenient and more self-serving.
sympathy.zh: 他们是否赢得了这种权利。他们的同情心是真实的，还是仅仅出于某种更方便、更自私的考量。

synthetic.en: It was quite painful to listen to. Today, synthetic speech is almost indistinguishable from a real human voice.
synthetic.zh: 听起来相当痛苦。如今，合成语音几乎与真实的人类声音无法区分。

synthetic.en: And then there are the synthetic ingredients, which allow perfumers to create scents that don’t exist in nature, like the smell of fresh linen or a salty ocean breeze.
synthetic.zh: 还有合成成分，它们使调香师能够创造出自然界中不存在的气味，比如新鲜亚麻布的气味或咸咸的海风。

synthetic.en: From the ancient temples of Mesopotamia to the laboratories of modern perfumers, from the rarest natural ingredients to the synthetic molecules designed to mimic them, perfume is much more than just a pleasant smell.
synthetic.zh: 从美索不达米亚的古代神庙到现代调香师的实验室，从最稀有的天然成分到旨在模仿它们的合成分子，香水远不止是一种令人愉悦的气味。

symmetry.en: This system would retain the 12-month format we’re familiar with but introduce regularity and symmetry within the year.
symmetry.zh: 这个系统将保留我们熟悉的 12 个月格式，但在一年内引入了规律性和对称性。

symmetry.en: The building is famous for its near-perfect symmetry.
symmetry.zh: 这座建筑以其近乎完美的对称性而闻名。

sympathize.en: The same way there's like the Michelle Thomas School of Language Learning and on that one what they do is you listen to a teacher talking to a student they're not teaching you you're not expected to remember or memorize anything you just listen to a student stumbling over the language it's a better way to learn because you yourself don't feel flustered you're being tested graded oh so you're not in your own head as much correct you're not in your own head and you're just you might even be laughing at the student or you might be agreeing with the teacher or vice versa or sympathizing with the student but because you are a passive observer you can be more objective about it and you aren't threatened or fearful and you can learn better and coming back to the original point of you can't change people if you do want to change someone's behavior i i think the only effective way to do it is to compliment them when they do something you want not to positive yeah exactly not to insult them or be negative or critical when they do something you don't want and we can't help it it's obviously in our nature to criticize and i do it as well but it just reminds me that like when somebody does something praiseworthy don't forget to praise them like definitely go out of your way and it'll be genuine.
sympathize.zh: 同样，有Michelle Thomas语言学习法，在那门课上，他们做的是你听老师和学生交谈，他们不是在教你，你不被期望记住或背诵任何东西，你只是听学生在语言上磕磕绊绊。这是一种更好的学习方式，因为你自己不会感到慌乱，你没有被测试、打分。哦，所以你没有那么沉浸在自己的头脑里？正确，你没有沉浸在自己的头脑里，你可能甚至在嘲笑那个学生，或者你可能在同意老师，反之亦然，或者同情学生，但因为你是一个被动的观察者，你可以更客观地看待它，你没有受到威胁或恐惧，你可以学得更好。回到最初的观点，你无法改变别人，如果你确实想改变某人的行为，我认为唯一有效的方法是在他们做你想做的事时称赞他们，而不是……积极的，是的，没错，而不是在他们做你不想要的事时侮辱他们或消极、批评。我们无法避免，批评显然是我们的天性，我也这样做，但这只是提醒我，当某人做了值得称赞的事时，别忘了称赞他们，一定要不遗余力，而且要是真诚的。

synthesis.en: And maybe in, you know, five years time you'll be like you know that thing that you said about the lessons and then i don't know it's cool that's like synthesis right it's this sort of blending of the reason i spend a lot of time in san francisco is because it's a gravitational attractor for the smartest people in the world and despite all the many problems the city had because it's mismanaged beyond belief it does just seem to pull in the young smart creative people not just the ones who are building technology but they're exploring every facet of life and they're weird and sometimes it's repulsive and it's bizarre but you talk to these people and you just see a very intelligent person coming at life in a completely different way putting it through the combinatorics of human dna which are uncountable and giving you a weird perspective that can twist your mind around and to do that you always have to be learning you you have you can't be the guru mentality If I'm with somebody and they're listening to every word I say and hanging on it, that's not interesting for me.
synthesis.zh: 也许五年后你会说，‘你知道你当时说的关于那些教训的事……’，我不知道，这很酷，这就是综合，对吧？这就是融合。我花很多时间在旧金山的原因是，它对世界上最聪明的人有一种引力吸引，尽管这座城市有许多问题，因为它管理得极其糟糕，但它似乎确实吸引了年轻、聪明、有创造力的人，不仅仅是那些搞技术的人，他们还在探索生活的方方面面，他们很古怪，有时甚至让人反感，很离奇，但你和这些人交谈，你会看到一个非常聪明的人以完全不同的方式对待生活，将其放入人类DNA的组合中，这些组合是数不胜数的，并给你一个奇怪的视角，可以扭转你的思维。要做到这一点，你必须始终保持学习，你不能有导师心态。如果我和某人在一起，他们听我说的每一个字，并对此深信不疑，那对我来说没意思。
